Article Title: Tesla CEO Elon Musk: Department of War revenue for my companies is …
Article Text:
Elon Musk

Palmer Luckey says he is 'not representing Anduril'

What is Pentagon's Project Meridian

Anduril founder Palmer Luckey recently pushed back against a report that said two major US defence contractors would help lead a Pentagon project that could benefit them. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), Palmer Luckey said he is advising the project in a personal capacity and rejected the description of Anduril as one of the US Department of Defense's biggest contractors. The post soon caught the attention of Tesla CEO Elon Musk who replied to Luckey's post, saying government defence revenue makes up only a small part of the total revenue of his companies.“Dept of War revenue for my companies is close to a rounding error of total revenue. Probably around 3% of SpaceX’s December ARR and ~1% of all my companies combined,” Elon Musk said.In the X post, Palmer Luckey was responding to a Politico report about Project Meridian, a Pentagon initiative looking at how warfare could change in the future. “Why are you lying?” Luckey wrote in his post adding “I am not Anduril, I am advising in a personal capacity.”Luckey also challenged the report's description of Anduril as one of the Department of Defense's biggest contractors. “Even if this was an Anduril project, it is nuts to call 67th place one of the Department's biggest contractors.”He said the ranking was clear and questioned why the report had presented the information that way.“You know this isn't true, but presumably you start your story with this false claim for a reason.”In the post, Luckey also shared a table showing defence contractor revenue rankings in his X post. The table showed companies such as Lockheed Martin and RTX among the biggest defence contractors, while Anduril was ranked much lower. Luckey used the ranking to support his argument that describing Anduril as one of the Pentagon's biggest contractors was misleading.Project Meridian is aimed at studying possible changes in future warfare. The project is linked to a commission led by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth , with input from people including Palmer Luckey, Elon Musk and Newt Gingrich. The commission is expected to study future military and warfare trends and produce a report by January 2027.The project has raised concerns about whether people advising the Pentagon could benefit from future defence contracts.
Article Summary: Palmer Luckey says he is 'not representing Anduril' on Pentagon's Project Meridian. Tesla CEO Elon Musk says government defence revenue makes up only a small part of the total revenue of his companies. Project Meridian is aimed at studying possible changes in future warfare.

Article Title: ChatGPT for Teens: 5 features parents should know about, from homework help to screen time controls
Article Text:
Study Mode: guided learning instead of instant answers

Homework reminders that nudge teens away from shortcuts

Turning tough topics into quizzes and interactive visuals

Parental controls that set structure without constant monitoring

Smarter prompts can make revision genuinely more productive

As AI tools become a fixture in how teenagers study, OpenAI is positioning its ChatGPT for Teens offering as a way to support independent learning rather than simply hand over answers — pairing study-focused features with age-appropriate parental safeguards designed to address a common worry among parents: how to let teens use AI for homework without letting it do the work for them.At the center of ChatGPT for Teens is Study Mode, which turns a simple question into a more structured learning experience. Rather than jumping straight to a final answer, it breaks concepts down step by step, offers hints, asks follow-up questions, and checks a student's understanding along the way.Students are encouraged to use prompts like asking ChatGPT to show them where they went wrong, give a hint for the next step, or help them work through a problem without revealing the answer outright — shifting the interaction from "give me the answer" to "help me understand how to get there."To discourage teens from simply offloading assignments onto AI, ChatGPT includes homework reminders that kick in when it detects a teen may be trying to use the tool to complete an assignment outright. Instead of letting a prompt like "write my history assignment" go through as-is, the system is designed to redirect students toward exploring key arguments and building their response themselves, step by step, within Study Mode — framed as a gentle nudge toward using AI as a learning aid rather than a replacement for actual effort.For subjects that are hard to grasp through reading alone, teens can ask ChatGPT to convert a chapter into a quiz, generate practice questions, or explain a concept in a different way if the first explanation doesn't click. The platform also includes Learning Visualizations, which offer interactive ways to explore more than 70 core maths and science concepts — letting students actually see how formulas, graphs, and variables behave in real time, rather than relying purely on memorization.For parents, ChatGPT for Teens includes linked parental controls that don't require reading every conversation to maintain oversight. Parents can set Study Hours, during which new chats automatically open in Study Mode, and Quiet Hours, during which access to the app can be limited altogether.Beyond scheduling, parents can also manage specific features like voice mode and image generation, along with sensitive-content protections. In limited, high-risk situations involving serious self-harm concerns, the system is also designed to send parents a direct safety notification — a feature aimed at balancing a teen's need for independence with a parent's need to know when something serious may be happening.Beyond homework help, ChatGPT can also support structured exam revision. Teens are encouraged to ask it to quiz them on a chapter with increasingly difficult questions as they improve, build a 30-minute revision plan, test their recall by asking questions without access to their notes, or identify which areas need more review based on how they answered previous questions.Used this way, the tool is pitched less as a replacement for traditional studying and more as a way to make revision time more active and targeted, complementing — rather than substituting for — what students already learn from teachers and textbooks.
Article Summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT for Teens lets teens use AI to help them learn. Study Mode turns a simple question into a more structured learning experience. It offers hints, asks follow-up questions, and checks a student's understanding along the way.

Article Title: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates says technology has truly stunned him only three times in his life, and the third happened this year when he looked closely at...
Article Text:
​Bill Gates, who wrote code before most of Silicon Valley was born, names the AI tool that stunned him this year

Bill Gates says coding is where AI's progress surprised him most

Gates expects AI to reshape software engineering jobs first

Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates says technology has truly stunned him only three times in his life, and the third came this year when he looked closely at Anthropic's AI coding tool, Claude Code. The first was in 1980, when he saw a graphical user interface for the first time, the idea that went on to shape the modern personal computer. The second was in 2022, when OpenAI 's leaders came to his house to demonstrate what would soon become ChatGPT.Claude Code hit differently because of what it does. Gates wrote code long before he became one of the world's richest people, and he calls it the subject he knows best. "The idea that now these things are in a meaningful sense better than I am is like: What the hell?" he said in a recent interview.Gates's reaction carries weight because of where he started. He began programming as a teenager in Seattle, and in 1975 he co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen on the back of software they wrote themselves. For most of his life, writing good code was the skill that set him apart.He said that AI's recent improvements had far exceeded his expectations, and Claude Code was a big part of that shift. It was also one of the reasons he chose to speak out now.In a nearly 6,000-word essay published on his blog, Gates Notes, he warned that the transition to AI will be "one of the most turbulent times in human history," and that the world is not preparing for it.Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool. Developers can hand it programming tasks from the command line, desktop or mobile app, and it writes, edits and debugs code for them. Anthropic showcased it at its Code with Claude developer event in May.Gates has been tracking AI's impact on programmers for a while. Earlier this year, he wrote that AI already makes software developers at least twice as efficient, and that its rate of improvement was starting to disrupt job demand in software development.In his latest essay, he listed software engineering among the first fields likely to feel the effects, alongside sales, customer support and paralegal work. He did offer one caveat. As coding gets cheaper, demand for software could grow, so net job losses in the field may be smaller than elsewhere, as long as some tasks, such as design, are still better done by humans.Still, coming from someone who built a company on software, the admission stands out. The tool that shocked Gates this year did not beat him at something unfamiliar. It beat him at the thing he knows best.
Article Summary: Bill Gates says Claude Code, an AI coding tool, stunned him this year. He wrote code long before he became one of the world's richest people. "The idea that now these things are in a meaningful sense better than I am is like: What the hell?" he said.

Article Title: Elon Musk's 'tip' to tech CEOs: Best way to test 'safety' of your AI models is to put them on a Delta flight, as ...
Article Text:
Earlier this week, Elon Musk warned that Delta will ‘lose a lot of customers’

Elon Musk warns Delta will ‘lose a lot of customers’

Delta Airlines on why it rejected Elon Musk’s Starlink

Elon Musk has humorously suggested that the best way to test the safety of AI models is by placing them on a Delta flight, implying that the airline's in-flight WiFi is so unreliable it effectively cuts off internet access. Sharing a post on X (formerly Twitter), Musk wrote:“Best way to sandbox an AI is to put it on a Delta flight – it will have no chance of accessing the Internet!”. The comments come as Delta Airlines opted against Starlink in favour of Amazon Leo for in-flight internet service. According to latest reports, Delta CEO Ed Bastian cited Elon Musk as the reason to skip Starlink. An X user JonNYC allegedly cited the Delta CEO saying “We do not want to be with Elon Musk”.In a post on September 28, X user John LeFevre said that Delta's rival United Airlines Holdings Inc. had 600+ aircraft with Starlink. The figure represented approximately 36% of the airline's entire fleet. "Delta has zero, and no plans for it. People will book accordingly. RIP Delta," he wrote in the post. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk responded to the post writing: “Delta will lose a lot of customers”.Delta Airlines is reportedly targeting 2028 to start offering Leo in-flight Wi-Fi on about half of its fleet. As quoted in a post by X user Sawyer Meritt earlier this year, Delta Airlines explained why it chose Amazon’s Leo saying:“This agreement gives us the fastest and most cost-effective technology available to better connect the world today, and it deepens our work with a global leader that shares our ambition to build what’s next.”In a statement to PC Mag then, the airline said “The assertion in question is not accurate”, claiming that incorporating Delta Sync with Starlink would have been permitted under SpaceX's in-flight Wi-Fi agreement. It further stated that it want to deepen work with “a global leader that shares our ambition to build what’s next.”
Article Summary: Elon Musk suggests best way to test the safety of AI models is by placing them on a Delta flight. Comments come as Delta Airlines opted against Starlink in favour of Amazon Leo for in-flight internet service. According to latest reports, Delta CEO Ed Bastian cited Elon Musk as the reason to skip Starlink.

Article Title: The next thing Adidas wants to make bespoke is the foam itself
Article Text:
An early prototype of Adidas's printed foam at the APEX Lab in Herzogenaurach

A foot model recreated from APEX scan data, used to build Project R.A.P. footwear

Running shoes have spent a decade getting faster through chemistry

Adidas's printed foam changes how it compresses through its structure, not a new formula

The Futurecraft 4D midsole, printed by Carbon as a lattice rather than moulded from foam. (Picture: Adidas)

Printed foam gets its behaviour from geometry

One of five printed foam versions Adidas made in three weeks.

The printed foam's underside, with openings that change in size and density from heel to toe.

Without a mould, foam can be remade for every athlete

Adidas's printed foam prototypes, which can be remade for each athlete without a mould.

Running-shoe foam has changed a great deal over the past decade, but it is still made in moulds, and a moulded midsole behaves the same way for every runner who wears that size. Adidas has been 3D-printing midsoles for close to a decade to get around that, though it has printed them from resin rather than foam.At its headquarters in Herzogenaurach, Adidas has now shown foam that comes out of a printer. It was the final stop at the APEX Lab during Home of Innovation, the company's name for a tour through the labs where athletes test products most people won't see for another year or two. Chief Creative Officer Alasdhair Willis calls it "a future continuously being built." APEX, short for Athlete Product Excellence, is the elite-only room where Adidas makes bespoke products for its biggest names.Most of the tables there dealt with how a shoe gets customised to a single athlete. One covered the profile APEX builds before anything is made: 3D body and foot scans, pressure mapping and gait analysis, the process behind boots and shoes made for Lionel Messi, Anthony Edwards, Noah Lyles and Alexander Zverev.Another held Project R.A.P., short for Radical Athlete Perception, Adidas's 3D-printed footwear platform.Its lattice boots are made from an athlete's scan data and worn in MLS matches by Philadelphia Union's Cavan Sullivan, and its basketball shoes by Brooklyn Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr.The last table came with a warning. Mateo, the designer behind it, said the project was at a very early stage, much further from production than R.A.P., and that the group was the first outside Adidas to see it. What he showed was printed foam, in structures that could be tuned in ways a moulded midsole cannot.Foam sits under almost every athletic shoe, but running is where the race to improve it has been fought most openly. For most of the last decade, progress in running-shoe cushioning has been a materials race. EVA, the light and cheap foam that sat under most shoes for years, gave way to expanded TPU, which Adidas brought to market as Boost in 2013. The next jump came from PEBA-based foams, which are lighter and return more energy, and which now sit under most elite racing shoes.Each step came from a lab working on the formula. A better foam meant a new polymer, a new blend or a new way of expanding it. Engineers could shape a midsole, stack layers or add a carbon plate, but the foam inside a moulded midsole behaves more or less the same throughout. Changing how it compresses has meant changing what it is made of.There is a practical reason for that. Foam midsoles are moulded, and a mould can only produce shapes that can be pulled back out of it. Complex internal structures are off the table, so the chemistry has had to carry most of the load.Adidas has found a way around that limit before. In 2017 it introduced Futurecraft 4D with Carbon, a printed midsole that gets its cushioning from a lattice structure, and 2021's 4DFWD added bowtie-shaped cells coded to compress forward under vertical impact. Those midsoles are printed as an elastomeric lattice, not foam in the EVA or Boost sense, so Adidas has been able to shape cushioning through geometry for some years, though never in foam.Mateo described printed foam as a combination of two things. From additive manufacturing it takes precision, control and customisation. From foam it keeps lightness, energy return and deformation, which he called a fancy word for how squishy it is. Adidas had to develop a new additive method to make it, though Mateo didn't say what the base material is.He was wearing one of the structures, so he walked up and down beside the table to show it working. This design is meant to maximise vertical deformation, meaning how far the foam compresses under load, and it does that by collapsing forward as the runner moves. You could see the cells fold in a set direction rather than squashing evenly, as a moulded slab would.The idea of a midsole that folds forward will be familiar from 4DFWD, which produced that movement with printed resin. The structure Mateo was wearing does it in foam, with the arrangement of its cells deciding how it compresses. He said this design was only one example, and a different structure could be optimised for weight, or built for walking rather than running, from the same material. A basketball shoe has to absorb heavy landings and support sharp cuts, while a walking shoe needs comfort over hours rather than speed over minutes. If the structure decides how the foam behaves, one printed material could in principle be shaped for each of those jobs.Geometry becomes more useful once it can be adjusted for an individual. Mateo said the lab can collect an athlete's pressure data, kinematics and foot scans, and then tune the structures to that athlete. That hasn't been possible with foam before, because a moulded midsole comes out the same for everyone in a size. APEX already profiles athletes across football, basketball, tennis and running, so the data needed to shape foam for one person is being collected well beyond runners.Speed matters as much as precision. Three weeks before the session, Mateo was at the factory where the samples on the table were made, and he produced five versions of the structure, each tuned differently. The process he described was simple: make a pair, test it with the athlete in the lab, adjust it, make another pair, and narrow down to the best shoe for that athlete.Alexander Taylor, Adidas's Senior Vice President of Innovation Design & Concepts, who was leading the group, put that pace in context. With conventional manufacturing, each change means working on moulds, and the structures on Mateo's table could not be moulded in the first place. Mateo has practically been living at the factory for the past three or four months, Taylor said, because the project now moves as quickly as he can test it. The shoes also look different, since the process produces shapes nothing from a mould would.For now, the project is being judged by how the structures behave rather than by numbers. Mateo didn't share energy-return figures to compare against moulded foams, and at this stage there may not be finished ones to share.Printed foam is still a long way behind R.A.P., which already has boots on an MLS pitch. If it follows the same path, its first wearers will be the athletes whose profiles are already on file at APEX, a few steps from the table where it was shown.
Article Summary: Adidas has been 3D-printing midsoles for close to a decade to get around that. It has printed them from resin rather than foam. At its headquarters in Herzogenaurach, Adidas has now shown foam that comes out of a printer.

Article Title: In 2018, Elon Musk donated $480,350 for Flint school water filters; four years later, redesigned systems allowed students to drink from fountains again after years of relying on alternative supplies
Article Text:
In 2018, Elon Musk donated $480,350 for Flint school water filters; four years later, redesigned systems allowed students to drink from fountains again after years of relying on alternative supplies

How the new water filters work

Why did the project take four years

For four years, students at Flint Community Schools relied on bottled and delivered water instead of drinking directly from school fountains. That is now changing after new ultraviolet water filtration systems were installed and tested across the district. The project dates back to 2018, when Elon Musk donated $480,350 to help install water filtration stations following the Flint water crisis. The upgraded systems are designed to remove lead, bacteria and other metals from water before it reaches students. District officials say testing found no detectable lead or harmful bacteria after filtration, allowing the drinking stations to be used again.A total of 130 filtration stations have been installed across Flint's 11 schools and administration building. The systems use three stages of filtration. Water first passes through an activated carbon filter designed to remove lead, copper and other particles. It then goes through an ultrafilter to remove most bacteria. Finally, ultraviolet light is used to kill remaining bacteria and viruses.Testing found lead levels before filtration varied by school. The highest average was 219 parts per billion (ppb) at Accelerated Learning Academy, while one test at Scott Elementary recorded 620 ppb.The US Environmental Protection Agency's recommended action level is 15 ppb.After filtration, tests found no detectable lead or harmful bacteria at the tested sites.The stations were installed during the 2019-20 school year, but researchers found problems with the original filters during testing. The systems produced inconsistent results and were not certified to meet National Sanitation Foundation standards.Researchers later redesigned the systems and began testing new units in 2021.The Community Foundation of Greater Flint led the project, partnering with local organisations and researchers. Musk made the donation through his Musk Foundation, adding to its support for Flint’s recovery after the water crisis.Superintendent Kevelin Jones said students can now drink from the hydration stations, but the district will continue providing bottled water for the rest of the school year as some families may still have concerns.“I am very excited,” Superintendent Kevelin Jones said. “It was about four years ago where we were talking about this, and this was in the early stages. ... To see that it came into fruition and our scholars can now drink water out of those hydration stations is a win for us,” Jones said.The district also plans regular testing and filter replacements to monitor water quality.
Article Summary: In 2018, Elon Musk donated $480,350 for Flint school water filters. Four years later, redesigned systems allowed students to drink from fountains again. The upgraded systems are designed to remove lead, bacteria and other metals from water before it reaches students. District officials say testing found no detectable lead or harmful bacteria after filtration.

Article Title: Larry Ellison bought eight homes near his Florida mansion, quite purchase made several residents upset, making homeowners association adopt restrictions
Article Text:
​Larry Ellison bought eight homes near his Florida mansion, quite purchase made several residents upset, making homeowners association adopt restrictions

Larry Ellison’s secret house hunt

Housing for tutors and domestic Staff

Limits after community backlash

Rising trend of Billionaire staff compounds

Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison has quietly acquired eight residential properties inside a single gated Florida development, spending nearly $10 million to house household staff and private tutors within commuting distance of his primary oceanfront estate, a report has said. The buying spree occurred over a matter of weeks in 2023 across Palm Meadows Estates, a 288-home community in West Boynton Beach located about 30 minutes from Ellison’s landmark Manalapan compound.As per a report by The Wall Street Journal, the acquisition unsettled several neighbours, prompting the community's homeowners association (HOA) to pass formal ownership caps to block single buyers from amassing large property clusters in the future.The acquisition drive started in March 2023 when Palm Meadows resident and LuxeIQ broker Kimmie Cruz was contacted by an outside agent seeking access to local listings for an undisclosed buyer looking to purchase roughly ten homes. The buyers focused on single-story ranch layouts, expanding their interest to properties not listed on the open market. That reportedly prompted Cruz to approach homeowners directly, pitching the opportunity of a verified cash buyer ready to close without standard listing hurdles.The buyer’s identity surfaced shortly after, when the 82-year-old tech billionaire toured the neighbourhood with his personal security guards. An LLC tied to Ellison closed on all eight properties across May and June 2023, spending roughly $10 million, according to county real estate filings cited by the publication.For some residents, the sudden purchases resulted in profits. For example, a family offloaded their three-bedroom, 2,100-square-foot house for $1.2 million – more than double the $567,000 they paid for it in 2019.The Palm Meadows homes stand in contrast to Ellison’s primary residence. While his flagship estate is a palatial trophy property, the Boynton Beach residences are conventional suburban homes with private yards and occasional pools.Sources familiar with the arrangement told The Wall Street Journal that the houses accommodate key staff who manage the billionaire’s daily operations, including educators instructing some of the five children he shares with his wife, Jolin Ellison. At the main Manalapan compound, dedicated spaces are set aside for homeschooling older children, who learn several languages under multiple private instructors.Residents report several staff members drive Tesla vehicles, and municipal records indicate building permits were filed to install Tesla Powerwall energy units across all eight homes following the purchase. (Ellison sat on Tesla’s board of directors from 2018 to 2022.)The concentration of properties under a single corporate owner drew friction from within the gated enclave, which features 24-hour manned gatehouses, a community clubhouse and water views from every lot. Uneasy about having a cluster of staff-occupied houses operated by an outside LLC, community members raised objections.According to Cruz, the Palm Meadows homeowners association enacted new ownership restrictions designed to stop similar bulk purchases.Ellison’s move highlights a growing pattern among ultra-wealthy executives, hedge fund founders and public figures who purchase off-site residential clusters for domestic employees. High-cost real estate markets make it difficult for essential staff, such as chefs, nannies, security personnel and estate managers, to reside within a practical driving distance.Housing staff in separate suburban quarters allows high-profile employers to maintain personal seclusion at their primary residences.
Article Summary: Larry Ellison bought eight homes near his Florida mansion, spending nearly $10 million to house household staff and private tutors. The buying spree occurred over a matter of weeks in 2023 across Palm Meadows Estates, a 288-home community in West Boynton Beach. The acquisition unsettled several neighbours, prompting the community's homeowners association to pass formal ownership caps to block single buyers.

Article Title: OpenAI fires three researchers, company confirms sacking; shares what investigations that led to termination revealed
Article Text:
OpenAI fires three researchers, company confirms sacking; shares what investigations that led to termination revealed

Alleged sharing of information with AI safety group

The connection to the Hugging Face breach

Part of a bigger reckoning inside OpenAI

A moment of mounting pressure on AI safety practices

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has terminated three researchers from its safety team after an internal investigation concluded that they violated company policies governing access to and handling of sensitive information, according to a company statement and a Wall Street Journal report. The ChatGPT maker confirmed that the employees were dismissed following a probe into the handling of confidential company data. "We have parted ways with three individuals for violating our policies on accessing and handling sensitive company information," an OpenAI spokesperson said. "Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work."According to a Wall Street Journal report, the three researchers are Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, all of whom worked on safety and alignment-related efforts at the company.The report said the researchers were accused of sharing confidential company information with third-party AI safety organisations, including nonprofit research groups involved in evaluating advanced AI systems.One of the dismissed employees, Tomek Korbak, had publicly said he served as OpenAI's technical contact for AI safety organisations METR and Redwood Research during an investigation into a recent AI security incident involving OpenAI models.The other two researchers, Wang and Balesni, worked on AI alignment, a field focused on ensuring AI systems behave in accordance with human intentions and safety objectives. Neither of the affected employees immediately commented on the dismissals, according to the report.The firings are directly tied to OpenAI's response to a string of recent security incidents in which its AI agents escaped containment, including an incident in which one of its models hacked AI platform Hugging Face. In the aftermath of that breach, OpenAI allowed staff from AI safety nonprofit METR, along with a contracted staff member from Redwood Research, to work inside its offices for six days to investigate how its models had behaved. METR later published a report based on what it learned during that access.Korbak, one of the three fired researchers and a member of OpenAI's safety team, has said he served as the company's technical point of contact for Redwood Research and METR throughout their investigation into the Hugging Face incident. The other two terminated employees, Wang and Balesni, worked on alignment — the broader effort to ensure AI models behave in ways humans actually intend.The firings come as OpenAI works to investigate a range of agent security incidents uncovered in recent months and address the underlying safety issues behind them. Just this week, the company scrapped the planned launch of a new AI model, GPT-6.1 Astra, specifically over safety concerns, underscoring how seriously these incidents are being treated internally.In response to the broader wave of security failures, OpenAI says it has implemented a new monitoring system designed to catch AI-agent misbehavior more quickly, started requiring engineers to apply stronger security guardrails when testing its AI systems, and committed to sharing more information publicly when its models behave badly.The firings land at a moment when major AI labs are facing growing pressure to submit their technology for independent safety testing. Just last month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said his company would allow outside evaluators like METR to verify its adherence to safety measures and assess model alignment — a step OpenAI had also taken, at least temporarily, in granting METR and Redwood Research access following the Hugging Face breach.That same climate of concern has produced other high-profile moments in recent weeks. In early September, Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon publicly resigned, saying he didn't want to be part of a rush to build AI systems capable of improving themselves, citing fears that such systems could spiral out of control and pose a threat to humanity. Around the same time, Amodei wrote publicly that the risks posed by today's most advanced AI tools were too significant to justify continuing development at the current breakneck pace, calling for an industry-wide slowdown — a call that drew public agreement from both OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk.
Article Summary: OpenAI fires three researchers, company confirms sacking; shares what investigations that led to termination revealed. The researchers were accused of sharing confidential company information with third-party AI safety organisations. The firings are directly tied to OpenAI's response to a string of recent security incidents in which its AI agents escaped containment.

Article Title: Disney layoffs have already hit marketing, Pixar, ABC News and ESPN, but there may be more to come; here's the 'smaller team' memo reportedly sent by a top exec
Article Text:
Disney layoffs

‘Disney’s legal division facing job cuts’

Division heads and brands in focus

The Walt Disney Company is reportedly preparing plans to overhaul its expansive television business with an internal restructuring expected to trigger hundreds of layoffs and merge operations across separate creative divisions. Citing people familiar with the situation, The Wall Street Journal reported that the senior leadership at the company is shaping the details of the restructuring, which may not be completed until the close of the year. The review represents the latest initiative since former theme parks chief Josh D’Amaro stepped into the CEO role in March, seeking to cut through corporate fragmentation across the media empire.The report said that the planned television changes follow a steady series of workforce reductions that started under D'Amaro's predecessor, Bob Iger, during his second term as CEO. Over recent cycles, staff departures have impacted Pixar, marketing departments, ABC News, and ESPN. Earlier this week, Disney cut more than 300 employees, primarily across corporate human resources and IT functions.Additional staff reductions are also being prepared within Disney’s legal and global affairs division, a group that employs roughly 1,000 workers. In an internal staff memo initially reported by Deadline, Horacio Gutierrez, Disney’s chief legal and global affairs officer, notified employees that the division “will be a much smaller organisation than it is today,” pointing to progress in automation as a driver of the shift.The cost-cutting pressure essentially mirrors a broader industry reality: legacy studios are trimming budgets as digital streaming operations struggle to generate the robust profit margins once provided by cable subscriptions. In response to changing consumer viewing, D’Amaro has pushed the company toward operating as a cohesive digital entertainment system rather than a collection of separate cable entities.The strategy has brought significant leadership moves. For example, last month, D’Amaro appointed former YouTube executive Adam Smith as chairman of streaming and brought in Silicon Valley veteran Karandeep Anand as chief technology officer (CTO), marking a level of seniority for pure tech executives at Disney.In August, the company opened a voluntary early-retirement package for executives aged 50 and older with at least a decade of tenure, holding off on finalising the television roadmap until participation numbers were tallied.A central aim of the planned TV reorganisation is aligning production teams around how modern streaming viewers watch content, rather than preserving traditional broadcast structures established decades ago.Addressing the strategy at a Bloomberg event on Thursday (October 1), Disney president and chief creative officer Dana Walden described the shift toward tighter coordination.“There is a need to constantly evaluate how you’re structured and how big is the organization,” Walden said, noting that Disney is taking operations that previously ran independently and “centralising as a television business, not a bunch of silos.”The reorganisation is being directed by Disney Entertainment Television Chairman Debra OConnell, who reports directly to Walden. Her oversight spans an extensive portfolio of production brands and development teams, including assets brought in through Disney's 2019 purchase of 21st Century Fox, including ABC Entertainment, 20th Television, Hulu Originals, Disney Kids & Family, National Geographic Content and Freeform.Currently, each unit retains its own leadership team to develop and produce shows for Disney+, Hulu, legacy linear channels, and third-party distributors. Insiders indicate that the coming consolidation is likely to impact some of the executives running these individual groups.
Article Summary: The Walt Disney Company is reportedly preparing plans to overhaul its expansive television business. An internal restructuring is expected to trigger hundreds of layoffs and merge operations across separate creative divisions. The review represents the latest initiative since former theme parks chief Josh D'Amaro stepped into the CEO role in March.

Article Title: Apple removes Bitchat app from India App Store 'after government order'
Article Text:
The app's developer and Twitter co-founder, Jack Dorsey, attached Apple’s notice to his post on X (Photo: Reuters).

NEW DELHI: Apple has removed Jack Dorsey-backed decentralised messaging app Bitchat from its India App Store following a government direction. Dorsey shared a screenshot of Apple’s communication on X, which said the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) had sought the app’s removal under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000.According to the notice shared by Dorsey, the government told Apple that the app included content that was illegal in India and directed the company to make it unavailable to users in the country. Apple said in its communication that Bitchat would continue to remain available in other territories.The company also said that Bitchat’s TestFlight version, which allows developers to distribute beta versions of apps to users for testing, would no longer be available in India.Bitchat differs from conventional messaging platforms because it does not necessarily require users to connect to the internet or rely on centralised servers. The app uses Bluetooth-based mesh networking, allowing nearby devices to communicate directly with each other and relay messages across a network of connected devices.Its decentralised architecture and ability to enable communication even when conventional internet access is unavailable have brought the app under regulatory scrutiny in India.The latest removal means iPhone users in India can no longer download the app through the official App Store. Apple did not respond to queries sent by TOI on the government direction or the reasons cited for removing Bitchat from its India store.The order comes a day after protests were organised in Delhi and Mumbai by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). The app, which can function without internet connectivity, had also faced a government takedown move in July, before again becoming available.
Article Summary: Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey shared a screenshot of Apple’s communication on X. The government told Apple that the app included content that was illegal in India. Apple said in its communication that Bitchat would continue to remain available in other territories. The order comes a day after protests were organised in Delhi and Mumbai.

Article Title: US FAA clears Boeing 737 MAX software issue, removes hurdle for MAX 10
Article Text:
WestJet first found the software issue

Boeing working on another software update

The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has cleared a software issue affecting some Boeing 737 MAX flight computers, saying it does not pose a safety concern, reports Reuters. The decision removes a major hurdle for certification of the 737 MAX 10, Boeing's largest MAX variant, which has faced delays for years. The FAA said an expert panel found that pilots would retain full control of the aircraft if the issue occurred and would receive clear warnings. The software problem could prevent pilots from using automated flight guidance during a specific landing situation. The FAA had delayed MAX 10 certification earlier this week while it reviewed the issue.As per the Reuters report, the FAA's Corrective Action Review Board met in Seattle on October 1 to examine the software issue. The regulator said the panel's decision was based on the fact that “pilots retain full ⁠control of the aircraft and the indications to the flight crew are clear and unambiguous.”The FAA said the software issue could prevent pilots from accessing automated flight guidance during an unusual landing situation.It could also increase pilot workload during a go-around, when a pilot stops a landing and climbs again to make another landing attempt.Canadian airline WestJet discovered the problem during an entry-into-service test flight nearly two years ago. The airline said the plane's vertical navigation mode, which helps automate the aircraft's vertical flight path, switched off during an approach.WestJet uses the affected U14.1 software on its MAX aircraft and is expected to receive the MAX 10 early next year.“WestJet has received no reports of this condition occurring during normal line operations,” the airline said in a staff memo seen by Reuters. “Very few occurrences have been reported by other operators using U14 or U14.1 because the condition requires a specific sequence of events.”Boeing said it will continue to follow the FAA's lead while its engineers work on the next software update. The company is also working with airlines on a procedure that would allow pilots “to re-enable automated vertical navigation should this situation occur.”The FAA said it will issue a Special Airworthiness Information Bulletin to US airlines and foreign aviation regulators to make them aware of Boeing's guidance.As per the report, the FAA's decision could allow the Boeing 737 MAX 10 to be certified later this month, in line with earlier expectations.
Article Summary: FAA has cleared a software issue affecting some Boeing 737 MAX flight computers. The decision removes a major hurdle for certification of the 737 MAX 10, Boeing's largest MAX variant. The FAA said an expert panel found that pilots would retain full control of the aircraft if the issue occurred.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael Dell: If you don't want to make mistakes, I doubt you will be super successful because failure is the best teacher
Article Text:
Quote of the day

“If you don't want to make mistakes, I doubt you will be super successful because failure is the best teacher. Also very important to learn from mistakes and not repeat them!” Michael Dell

What the quote actually means

What went wrong:

Why did it happen:

What could have been done differently:

What information was missing:

What can be changed next time:

How can the same mistake be avoided:

What did the failure teach us:

Why this mindset is more important than it seems

Mistakes are made by everyone. They can happen when you’re learning something new, making decisions at work or pursuing a bigger goal. Mistakes are often viewed as failures, but they can also be lessons failure simply cannot be. We’ve got to find out what went wrong and learn from that.That's the idea behind a quote by Michael Dell, the founder and CEO of Dell Technologies, who said: “If you don't want to make mistakes, I doubt you will be super successful because failure is the best teacher. Also very important to learn from mistakes and not repeat them!” The thought highlights how mistakes and failures can become valuable learning experiences when people take the time to understand them and avoid repeating the same errors.Dell's statement is closely connected to the idea that mistakes are part of learning. Trying to avoid every possible mistake can mean avoiding situations with uncertainty, experimentation, or opportunities to learn something new.Failure can provide information about what did not work. It can reveal weaknesses in an idea, process, or decision and give people a chance to make changes before trying again.But the quote is not simply about accepting failure. What matters more is what happens after a mistake.If the same mistake repeats without understanding what caused it, the experience provides little value.For example, if a business launches a product that fails to attract customers, simply accepting that the product didn't work isn't enough. The company can look at who the product was designed for, what customers expected, how it was marketed, what competitors offered and where the product fell short.Some questions that can help you learn from mistakes include:Identifying the specific problem can make it easier to understand what needs to change.Looking beyond the immediate mistake can help you identify the underlying reason.Considering alternative approaches can provide useful lessons for future decisions.A mistake may happen because you overlooked an important piece of information or it wasn't available at the time.Turning a lesson into a specific change can make it more useful than simply acknowledging the mistake.Creating a new process, checklist or approach can help prevent the problem from happening again.Not every failed attempt produces the same lesson, so identifying the broader takeaway can help apply the experience elsewhere.It is easy to see mistakes as something to be avoided. But a fear of making mistakes can also make people less willing to experiment, take calculated risks or try unfamiliar approaches.That is where Dell's idea becomes important. A mistake does not automatically lead to success, but it can provide information you can use to improve. The value of failure depends largely on whether people examine what happened and apply what they learned.The same approach can apply to everyday challenges. At work, for example, a project may miss a deadline or fail to deliver the expected results. Treating the outcome only as a failure may not help the team improve. Looking at what caused the delay, which assumptions were wrong, and what could change in the next project can turn the experience into a useful lesson.The idea also changes how we view success. Success doesn’t have to be a straight line with no bumps. It’s about trying things out, learning from what you try, and making adjustments along the way.Dell's quote therefore isn't saying failure should be pursued for its own sake. It is that mistakes can become valuable when people learn from them. Understanding what went wrong, making changes and avoiding the same error can turn a setback into an opportunity to improve.
Article Summary: Michael Dell said: “If you don't want to make mistakes, I doubt you will be super successful because failure is the best teacher. Also very important to learn from mistakes and not repeat them!” A mistake does not automatically lead to success, but it can provide information you can use to improve.

Article Title: Vi Business partners with Cisco to expand Hybrid SD-WAN offerings for enterprises
Article Text:
Focus on cloud, security and network management

Vi Business, the enterprise arm of Vodafone Idea, has partnered with Cisco to strengthen its Hybrid SD-WAN portfolio as enterprises increasingly seek secure and scalable networking solutions to support cloud adoption, distributed operations and AI-driven workloads.The collaboration combines Cisco Meraki's cloud-managed networking and secure multi-WAN capabilities with Vi Business' managed connectivity services, aiming to help enterprises modernise their network infrastructure through hybrid networking, integrated security and multi-cloud connectivity.According to the company, the partnership comes at a time when enterprise demand for software-defined wide area networking (SD-WAN) is rising rapidly. Industry estimates project India's SD-WAN market to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 20.5% to reach $14.6 billion by 2031.Vi Business launched its Hybrid SD-WAN solution in 2023 to help enterprises transform traditional wide area networks by combining SD-WAN technology, security capabilities and multi-cloud integration through a managed services model.Under the partnership, the solution will be powered by Cisco Meraki, enabling enterprises to manage their networks through a single dashboard with application-aware routing, performance monitoring, built-in security, Wi-Fi and cellular connectivity features.The telecom operator said customers will benefit from a fully managed service that includes nationwide connectivity, proactive monitoring, lifecycle management and a single point of contact for support and operations. The offering is being delivered through a service-based model, which allows enterprises to avoid upfront capital expenditure while scaling network infrastructure as business requirements evolve.Commenting on the partnership, M P Sunil Kumar, Chief Enterprise Business Officer at Vodafone Idea, said enterprises are increasingly looking for networking solutions that align with evolving business objectives. "By integrating advanced cloud-managed SD-WAN, wired and wireless networking and built-in security, we enable enterprises to centrally manage distributed networks while radically simplifying operations," Kumar said.He added that the combination of nationwide connectivity, managed services and end-to-end support would help organisations build resilient and scalable networks.Ashok Shivashankar, Managing Director, Partner Organization, Cisco India & South Asia, said enterprise networks must increasingly be designed for agility, scalability and security in an AI-first environment."Together with Vi Business, we are helping enterprises modernise their networks with a managed Hybrid SD-WAN solution that enables greater agility, scalability and operational efficiency while accelerating digital transformation," Shivashankar said.The partnership strengthens Vi Business' push into enterprise digital transformation services as organisations continue to invest in cloud infrastructure, remote operations and AI-enabled business applications.
Article Summary: Vi Business, the enterprise arm of Vodafone Idea, has partnered with Cisco. The collaboration combines Cisco Meraki's cloud-managed networking and secure multi- WAN capabilities with Vi Business' managed connectivity services. Vi Business launched its Hybrid SD-Wan solution in 2023 to help enterprises transform traditional wide area networks.

Article Title: TRAI in October 2026 notification to Airtel, Reliance Jio and Vodafone-Idea: Clearly display these prepaid packs and special tariff vouchers; gives deadline
Article Text:
Representative Image

What TRAI order says

TRAI order on STVs

"Provided also that the service provider shall offer Special Tariff Vouchers (STVs) with appropriate reduction in tariff, exclusively for Voice and SMS for:

(i) validities corresponding to each validity period of thirty days and less than thirty days for STV being offered for Voice, SMS and data, whether with or without value added services and;

(ii) validity renewable on the same date of every month and if the date of such renewal is not available in a month, the date of renewal shall be the last date of that month and;

(iii) at least one STV with validity more than (i) and (ii) above, corresponding to the validity period of STVs being offered for Voice, SMS and data, whether with or without value added services. "

Deadline for compliance

India's Telecom regulator TRAI does not seem to be happy with the way the country's mobile service providers -- Reliance Jio, Airtel and Vodafone-Idea -- show prepaid packs and special tariff vouchers. In a notification issued recently, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has asked mobile service providers to prominently display mandatory recharge plans and special tariff vouchers on their websites, mobile apps and exclusive points of sale. These regulations are called the Telecom Consumers Protection (Thirteenth Amendment) Regulations, 2026.TRAI maintains that it has come with new guidelines after receiving complaints from consumers. It further claims that the regulator too has verified that the telecom operators had placed plans on their websites and apps in a manner that they were not easily visible. In a similar notification, earlier this year, TRAI had also mandated telecom operators to issue special tariff vouchers for voice calls and SMS at a lower cost, as they will not come bundled with data services. Under the mandate, telecom operators will have to issue Special Tariff Vouchers (STVs) for voice calls and SMS only, similar to the existing ones that come bundled with data, voice calls and SMS, carrying validity of 30 days or less.For those unaware, an STV works like a booster recharge for prepaid mobile customers, allowing them to avail of extra benefits by paying an additional amount through these vouchers, like making international calls at lower rates, adding the benefit of unlimited calls in the existing plan, among others.While some STVs offering data services are available for a validity of up to 365 days, TRAI's new regulation focuses on vouchers with a validity of 30 days and less. These rules are aimed to help people in rural areas and customers with low paying capacity. Trai has mandated that every telecom operator must offer at least one plan voucher, one Special Tariff Voucher and one combo voucher having a validity of thirty days."...the Authority...hereby directs all telecom service providers to...provide a separate and clearly visible tab or section titled "TRAI-Mandated Packs" containing different types of TRAI mandated vouchers, which shall be visible as the first tab on the prepaid recharge section on the websites and mobile apps of the service providers and shall also be prominently displayed on their other exclusive points of sale," the TRAI order says.The regulator, however, came across complaints from various subscribers to the different types of Trai-mandated vouchers on the websites and to the different types of Trai-mandated vouchers on the websites and mobile applications of the service provider."In some cases, these vouchers are placed under different categories or require consumers to navigate through multiple pages or screens to find them, as a result of which consumers are facing difficulty in locating and subscribing to the vouchers suitable to their requirementsẠạ the regulator said.Similar to Prepaid packs, TRAI acknowledged that upon examination of the websites and mobile applications of various telecom service providers, it was observed that Trai-mandated vouchers are neither displayed prominently nor are easily accessible.Telecom regulator has now directed Reliance Jio, Airtel and Vodafone-Idea to comply with the order within thirty days from the date of issuing the direction (October 1).
Article Summary: Telecom regulator has now directed Reliance Jio, Airtel and Vodafone-Idea to comply with the order within thirty days from issuing it. Trai has mandated that every telecom operator must offer at least one plan voucher, one Special Tariff Voucher and one combo voucher having a validity of thirty days.
