Article Title: Google ex-CEO Eric Schmidt: Best programmers don't write code anymore, they...
Article Text:
Eric Schmidt's idea of a top programmer goes to bed at 7 PM

The best programmers won't be replaced by AI—they'll become even more valuable

Schmidt says AI's real impact will be automating the 'boring' backbone of business

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says the most valuable programmers in the world have quietly redefined their job. They don't write code anymore. They write specifications, set evaluation criteria, hit run—and go to bed. It's a shift that Schmidt believes signals something much larger than a change in workflow—it's the beginning of AI reshaping how entire industries operate.Schmidt described a programmer at one of his startups who does exactly this. Every evening at 7 PM, he defines what he wants the AI to build, writes a test function to judge the output, and lets the system loose. Then he has dinner with his wife and goes to sleep. The AI churns through the night, finishing around 4 AM. By breakfast, the work is done. "This stuff would've taken me six months and 10 programmers at Google," Schmidt said. "This poor guy's sleeping."The natural assumption is that AI will make programmers obsolete. Schmidt thinks the opposite is true—at least for the elite ones. Top-tier engineers were always disproportionately valuable, worth roughly 10 times more than those just below them. That gap, he argued, is about to widen.The grunt work is disappearing, but the ability to orchestrate AI systems at scale—grasping parallelisation, defining the right constraints, judging when the output is good enough—is becoming the entire job.The real skill now isn't writing code, Schmidt suggested. It's framing the problem correctly and knowing what "good" looks like. "If you can define the evaluation function and you can let it run, and if you have enough hardware, you're inventing worlds," he said. AI systems at leading research labs are already handling a significant and growing share of programming work, making the engineers who direct them more critical, not less.Yet the bigger story, Schmidt argued, isn't about programmers at all. AI's largest economic payoff will come from automating the dull, expensive plumbing of corporate operations—billing, accounting, inventory management, delivery logistics—processes that silently drain billions from company budgets every year. "If anything, it's under-hyped because you are fundamentally automating businesses," he said at Harvard's John F. Kennedy Jr. Forum.He predicted artificial general intelligence could arrive as early as 2029, powered by recursive self-improvement—AI systems that learn and plan on their own, without waiting for human instruction. Schmidt also pointed to medicine, climate solutions, and engineering as fields where AI-driven automation could unlock breakthroughs that remain largely untapped today.
Article Summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says the most valuable programmers in the world have quietly redefined their job. They don't write code anymore. They write specifications, set evaluation criteria, hit run and go to bed. Schmidt says AI's real impact will be automating the 'boring' backbone of business operations.

Article Title: Elon Musk and Delta Airlines are fighting again; this time Tesla CEO predicts: Delta will lose a lot of ...
Article Text:
Delta backs Amazon's satellite service

Airline Wi-Fi becoming a competitive battleground

Whether Musk's prediction holds up remains to be seen

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has once again reignited his public criticism of Delta airlines CEO Ed Bastian and the connectivity strategy of the airline, predicting that Delta could lose customers after choosing Amazon’s satellite internet service instead of SpaceX’s Starlink. The latest exchange began after John LeFevre posted on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) that United Airlines had already equipped more than 600 aircrafts, or roughly 36% of its fleet, with Starlink connectivity, while Delta had no plans to adopt the service. Responding to LeFevre’s post, Musk wrote, “Delta will lose a lot of customers”.According to a report by TheStreet, earlier this year Delta opted to use Amazon’s Leo satellite internet service instead of Starlink and plans to begin installing the system on 500 aircrafts from 2028. The report also added that Musk earlier claimed that Delta wanted Starlink’s internet service to be routed through the airline’s own proprietary login portal, an arrangement SpaceX was unwilling to support. The Tesla and SpaceX chief also reportedly escalated the dispute by suggesting that Bastian could ultimately lose his job over the decision, following reports that the Delta chief did not want the airline associated with Musk personallyThe disagreement highlights intensifying competition in the in-flight connectivity market, where satellite internet is increasingly seen as a differentiating factor for airlines. The report noted that United Airlines has said customer satisfaction with Wi-Fi on Starlink-equipped flights is about twice as high as on aircraft using its previous systems. United aims to connect its entire fleet by the end of 2027.Meanwhile, American Airlines has also committed to installing Starlink on more than 500 narrowbody aircraft, with deployments set to begin in the first quarter of 2027.Analysts note there's currently no booking data showing travelers actively switching airlines specifically over Wi-Fi provider choice, meaning Musk's prediction remains speculative for now rather than backed by hard evidence.Still, the broader trend favors his argument to some degree: every additional airline that adopts Starlink adds pressure on holdouts like Delta, particularly as reviewers continue to praise Starlink's in-flight performance.Delta, for its part, is betting that Amazon's Leo service will prove competitive once its rollout begins in 2028 — leaving the real verdict on Musk's prediction to be settled by passengers, not social media posts, over the next couple of years.
Article Summary: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has reignited his public criticism of Delta airlines CEO Ed Bastian and the connectivity strategy of the airline. The latest exchange began after John LeFevre posted on social media platform X that United Airlines had already equipped more than 600 aircrafts, or roughly 36% of its fleet, with Starlink connectivity. Responding to the post, Musk wrote, “Delta will lose a lot of customers”.

Article Title: Godfather of AI Yann LeCun does not believe that AI will kill humans; 'blames' humans for AI Agents hacking into companies' networks and government websites; says: “Those agents are doing exactly what
Article Text:
Godfather of AI Yann LeCun does not believe that AI will kill humans; 'blames' humans for AI Agents hacking into companies' networks and government websites; says: “Those agents are doing exactly what ...

Yann LeCun says AI risks are being exaggerated

Yann LeCun criticises AI safety warnings

Yann LeCun, widely known as the “godfather of AI”, does not believe artificial intelligence (AI) will wipe out humanity. Instead, LeCun says recent incidents in which AI agents hacked company networks and other systems were caused by poor human oversight and badly designed security systems. Speaking about the risks linked to AI agents, Yann LeCun said told Fortune: “Those agents are doing exactly what they’ve been asked to do,” adding that the systems were supposed to operate inside secure sandboxes. “They were supposed to be in sandboxes, but the sandboxes were leaky and horribly designed,” he said.Yann LeCun, who shared the 2018 Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio for their work on deep learning, said he has “zero concerns” about recent rogue AI incidents and is not worried “at all” about AI destroying humanity.He said incidents such as an OpenAI agent autonomously hacking Hugging Face could have been prevented through better system design and oversight. LeCun also argued that some AI labs do not have a strong enough understanding of cybersecurity. He said the risks from AI agents should be addressed through better safeguards rather than broad claims about AI becoming an existential threat.During the interaction, Yann LeCun has also criticised the growing focus on AI safety, particularly ideas linked to the effective altruism movement.He called the movement “super toxic” and a “complete disaster.”He also criticised warnings from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman that AI could pose serious risks to humanity. Amodei, LeCun said, is “honest”, but he accused him of supporting policies that could benefit large AI companies by making it harder for smaller competitors and open-source developers to compete.“Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman ‘saying, ‘AI can kill us all’ is incredibly destructive for everybody, including for the public who’s scared shitless,” LeCun said. He called such messaging “the worst marketing campaign you can possibly imagine.”
Article Summary: Yann LeCun does not believe that AI will kill humans. 'blames' humans for AI Agents hacking into companies' networks and government websites. “Those agents are doing exactly what they’ve been asked to do,” he said.

Article Title: Microsoft executive Ryan Roslansky, who served as LinkedIn chief, is leaving company: Read CEO Satya Nadella's memo
Article Text:
In pic: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella

Read Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella’s memo to employees on Ryan Roslansky’s exit

Microsoft executive Ryan Roslansky, who led the software company’s LinkedIn subsidiary for six years, will leave at the end of 2026. Satya Nadella , Microsoft’s CEO, announced the departure in a memo to the employees. The Redmond, Washington-based company has seen multiple leadership changes in recent months. The high-profile exit comes after gaming head Phil Spencer and Office leader Rajesh Jha both left this year, and Charlie Bell, the company’s head of security, took on a new role focused on engineering quality.Roslansky joined LinkedIn as product chief in 2009, when it was still a privately held company. Microsoft acquired LinkedIn for $27 billion in 2016. In 2020, Roslansky replaced Jeff Weiner as LinkedIn CEO. During Roslansky’s tenure, LinkedIn’s membership expanded from 700 million to 1.3 billion. Previously, he had held management roles at Yahoo and Glam Media.In 2025, Roslansky took on additional responsibility in Microsoft’s Office productivity software group. Earlier this year, Nadella named Roslansky and two other executives as leaders of the Microsoft 365 applications and the Copilot artificial intelligence platform, and Dan Shapero, LinkedIn’s chief operating officer (COO), became the professional social network’s CEO.After nearly 18 years at LinkedIn and Microsoft, Ryan Roslansky has decided to leave Microsoft and embark on his next chapter.As Ryan and I have been discussing our roadmap and work ahead, we felt this was the right moment for this change. Ryan will stay through the end of the calendar year as an advisor to me and will support on the transition.Ryan leaves the organization in a strong position. With Copilot, we are executing rapidly against our vision to build a new OS for work that spans every model, every form factor, and every task, with Office fully embedded in Copilot and vice versa! Over the past year, Ryan’s team has done critical work bringing together the product, engineering, and design foundations that have made this next phase possible. Last week’s launch was an important milestone in that journey, and the strong response from customers, partners, and the broader ecosystem reinforced both how far we’ve come and how much opportunity remains ahead.At LinkedIn, we remain focused on our core vision of creating economic opportunity for every member of the global workforce, helping our 1.3 billion members access the knowledge, insights, and opportunities they need to navigate rapidly changing professional and labor markets.Effective today we will make the following changes:Sumit Chauhan and Lan Ye will report to Charles Lamanna.Jon Friedman will report to Jacob Andreou.Dan Shapero will continue as CEO of LinkedIn and Mohak Shroff will continue in his role, both reporting to me.Over his nearly two decades at Microsoft, Ryan has helped shape how people around the world find opportunity, build their careers, and get their work done. I’ve always appreciated his clarity of thinking and I’m deeply grateful for everything Ryan has built, for the leaders and teams he has developed, and for his friendship and counsel.Please join me in thanking Ryan for his extraordinary contributions to LinkedIn and Microsoft, and in wishing him the very best in what comes next.SatyaWhat Ryan Roslansky told workers in a memoTeam,In 1996, as a college freshman, I taught myself to code so a few friends and I could help other students find a place to live around campus. I didn’t know much. I did know the internet was about to change how people found things, and I wanted to be as close to that as possible.In 2009, Jeff Weiner made me his first hire at LinkedIn. I’ve spent the nearly 18 years since working on a much bigger version of that same idea: helping people find opportunity, and then helping them do great work once they have it.This has (obviously) been the best professional experience of my life.As a product manager, I got to build dozens of features that are still around today (some good, some not so good!). When I became CEO in 2020, the world was months into a pandemic that changed what work even meant. Nobody hands you a playbook for that. This team wrote one anyway. Since then, LinkedIn has passed a billion members and nearly tripled its business, and every bit of that belongs to the people who built it.Last year, Satya asked me to help build the future of M365. Once again, the old rules didn’t apply. AI was rapidly changing how professionals work, and the world’s largest productivity suite needed to lead the way. That meant figuring out what Copilot, and the future of work, should look like as one ecosystem.We still have a ways to go, but the progress over the past year has been inspiring to watch. A lot of talented people set aside their own roadmaps to make that happen. Thank you. I know it wasn’t easy.Satya, thank you. When LinkedIn joined Microsoft, you gave us room to build, and then trusted many of us with a lot more. I’ve learned more from you than I can fit in an email, and I’m grateful for the friendship that came with it.All of which made this a hard decision. I know what it would take for me to lead the next phase of this work well: being in Redmond full time, every day. But my life and my family’s life are here in the Bay Area. My wife Leigh gives her time to more local organizations than I can keep track of. Our youngest daughter just started high school, and our dog Buddy remains deeply committed to the trails on the Peninsula!I thought about this for a long time. It’s the right call. The work now goes to leaders who are set up to take it further. I can’t wait to see what they do with it.Over the years, people have asked me what’s kept me so energized and motivated in this work. I think the answer is that I got to spend my career working where doing good and doing well are the same thing. In technology, that’s the best place to operate.Most companies start by focusing on doing well, so doing good becomes a compromise. It’s the last slide of the PowerPoint, or a separate .org. But when doing good is built into the product itself, it becomes a real competitive advantage. When we build valuable products, people find jobs, they hire, they learn skills, they start companies, they run companies. That creates value for members, customers and the world. And for our business too.Not many companies get to work this way, and not many people get the chance to build something like it. We do.That matters more now than it ever has. Technology will continue to touch every job on the planet, and the people building it will decide what kind of world it helps create. I can’t think of a better group to figure that out than the people reading this note.Thank you for the best 18 years I could have asked for.RR
Article Summary: Microsoft executive Ryan Roslansky, who led the software company’s LinkedIn subsidiary for six years, will leave at the end of 2026. Microsoft acquired LinkedIn for $27 billion in 2016. The Redmond, Washington-based company has seen multiple leadership changes in recent months. The exit comes after gaming head Phil Spencer and Office leader Rajesh Jha both left this year.

Article Title: Google Japan's Gboard Kurukuru keeps the keys moving so your fingers don't have to
Article Text:
Google's new keyboard brings the keys to you.

You can't buy Google's conveyor belt keyboard , but you can build one

Google Japan has a new keyboard out, and this time you don't go hunting for the keys because they come to you. The Gboard Kurukuru Version puts its keys on four little conveyor belts that keep rolling, and you simply tap the letter you want when it slides under your finger.There are 29 keys on each belt, so 116 in all. Capital and small letters get their own keys too, which means you never have to touch Shift.If you're worried about timing your taps, a voice calls out each key as it reaches a set point. Feeling confident? There's a speed mode that spins the belts faster. And if you miss your letter, well, you wait for it to come back around.It plays a lot like a rhythm game.The idea, Google says, is to make one-handed typing easier. On a normal keyboard your hand has to move around to find the keys, and that gets tiring fast with one hand, let alone one finger. Here the keys do the moving, so your other hand is free for the mouse or, as Google puts it, a cup of tea.The company even calls it a "Copernican revolution" in typing, and says you can build a second one if you want to type with both hands. "Kurukuru" loosely means spinning round and round in Japanese, which pretty much sums it up.As you'd expect, there's no buy option for this one. Google has instead put the whole design up on GitHub as an open-source project, so if you've got the parts and the patience, you can build one at home.This is the 15th keyboard Google Japan has dreamt up for October 1, a tradition that took over from its April Fools' jokes in 2021. The date is a little joke of its own, since 10/1 reads as 101, as in the old 101-key keyboard.Before this, we got the extra-long Gboard Bar, the wearable Gboard Caps and last year's Gboard Dial, which had you typing like you were dialling a rotary phone. Google says faster belts, longer and portable versions, and more colours could be next, so the wait for your next letter might get a bit shorter.
Article Summary: Gboard Kurukuru Version puts keys on four conveyor belts. You simply tap the letter you want when it slides under your finger. There are 29 keys on each belt, so 116 in all. Capital and small letters get their own keys too, so you never have to touch Shift.

Article Title: Chinese government to families of CEOs, CTOs and other top executives working in AI companies: You need permission to travel to ...
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

China expands restrictions to families of AI executives

Why China is restricting AI talent

Manus deal adds to China's concerns

China has expanded overseas travel restrictions for senior professionals working in its artificial intelligence and semiconductor sectors. The new measures are also affecting the families of some key executives. According to a Bloomberg report, families of CEOs, CTOs, and other top executives at strategically important private AI companies are now being told they need Beijing's permission to travel abroad. The restrictions mean that spouses and children of certain AI and chip executives may need government approval even for short overseas trips.The move is part of Beijing’s broader effort to prevent the outflow of critical technology, information and talent as China seeks to strengthen its position in AI and chipmaking. The latest measures widen existing travel restrictions already imposed on prominent AI professionals at companies including Alibaba and DeepSeek.The report cited people familiar with the matter, who said Chinese government agencies have begun notifying those affected by the expanded restrictions. Members include top startup founders and executives at companies operating in strategically important AI-related sectors.The new requirements do not amount to an outright travel ban. However, certain senior AI and semiconductor professionals and their immediate family members now need approval before travelling overseas.It remains unclear whether the requirement applies to the families of all professionals covered by the broader restrictions. Chinese government departments have already informed several people that their family members need to obtain clearance before travelling abroad, two people familiar with the matter said.Beijing has previously imposed travel restrictions on personnel considered important to national security, including researchers, nuclear scientists and executives at state-owned companies. Their families can also be affected.China's latest measures specifically target private-sector talent, reflecting the strategic importance of AI engineers, researchers, and executives to the country's technology ambitions.Much of China's leading AI talent emerged during the rapid development of generative AI following the launch of ChatGPT. Many of these researchers and engineers work for technology giants and private startups, making them an important part of China's efforts to develop advanced AI systems and semiconductor technologies.The restrictions aim to reduce the risk of sensitive knowledge and technology leaving the country, particularly as Beijing and Washington compete over advanced AI and chips.China has already restricted overseas travel for senior AI professionals working at private companies including Alibaba and DeepSeek. Bloomberg reported in May that the measures reflected Beijing's efforts to protect strategically important technology and talent.Beijing's concerns about losing AI talent and technology intensified following Meta Platforms' US$2 billion acquisition of Manus, an AI startup with Chinese roots.The Chinese government eventually ordered the US company to unwind the deal. Beijing also moved to restrict US investment in sensitive Chinese technology companies following the fallout.The latest restrictions are not necessarily connected directly to the Manus acquisition, according to Bloomberg. However, preventing the transfer of sensitive technology and talent remains an important policy objective for Beijing.China is also enforcing separate rules that took effect on September 15, including exit bans in cases involving criminal investigations and potential violations of the country's industrial and technological security.The government plans to add more individuals to the list of people subject to the restrictions over time, according to people familiar with the matter. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology did not respond to a request for comment.The broader restrictions could create additional pressure for Chinese AI professionals with international careers, as engineers and researchers may have to consider government approval requirements when travelling abroad.
Article Summary: China expands restrictions to families of AI executives. Restrictions mean spouses and children of certain AI and chip executives may need government approval even for short overseas trips. Move is part of Beijing’s broader effort to prevent the outflow of critical technology, information and talent.

Article Title: In 2024, Jeff Bezos' ex-wife MacKenzie Scott gave $30 million to a Silicon Valley housing nonprofit; a year later, it unveiled a 10-year plan to widen access to affordable homes in the Bay Area
Article Text:
The gift came through MacKenzie Scott's Yield Giving philanthropic fund

A year later: the 10-year plan takes shape

Real projects already benefiting

Part of a broader pattern of giving

In October 2024, Jeff Bezos’ ex-wife and philanthropist MacKenzie Scott, through her Yield Giving fund, donated $30 million to Housing Trust Silicon Valley, providing the largest individual gift in the nonprofit’s history. The unrestricted donation was aimed at helping the organisation expand affordable housing opportunities across the 14-county Bay Area, one of the most expensive housing markets in the United States. As per Housing Trust TV, announcing the gift, Noni Ramos, chief executive of Housing Trust Silicon Valley, said the funding would enable the organisation to accelerate efforts to create more equitable and affordable communities. The nonprofit indicated that the money could be used to strengthen its loan fund, expand existing housing programmes and launch new initiatives focused on affordability and housing equity.The gift, announced in October 2024, came through Mackenzie Scott's Yield Giving philanthropic fund and stood as the largest single donation from an individual in Housing Trust's history. Housing Trust CEO Noni Ramos described the unrestricted contribution as an incredible surprise the organization felt deeply honored and grateful to receive, noting that the trust placed in the organization also carries a responsibility to translate that generosity into meaningful, lasting impact for the communities it serves.Housing Trust's Board Chair, Joe Anzalone, framed the timing as especially significant, coming just as the organization was preparing to mark 25 years of funding affordable housing solutions. He pointed to the scale of Housing Trust's track record up to that point — having invested $615 million in the community, created more than 27,200 housing opportunities, and helped over 51,000 neighbors find affordable housing across the region, while helping leverage an additional $8.1 billion through its partners.Founded in 2000, Housing Trust was created through a partnership between affordable housing advocates, businesses, and public and private sector leaders and foundations, aimed at meeting the Bay Area's growing need for affordable housing solutions.Nearly a year after the initial gift, Housing Trust unveiled a detailed 10-year plan in September 2025 for how it intends to convert the $30 million into durable, long-term housing solutions across the region — a plan the organization says was shaped through input from staff, board members, and community stakeholders.The roadmap centers on five major initiatives designed to direct the gift toward both expanded housing opportunity and stronger organizational capacity over the coming decade. According to the plan, the funding will help accelerate Housing Trust's core lending work, expand homeownership assistance programs, fuel new policy and innovation efforts, and strengthen the organization's overall long-term impact.Concretely, that includes growing Housing Trust's core revolving loan fund and piloting new financing tools tailored specifically for developers. Michael Quinn, who leads much of this development-facing work at Housing Trust, described the approach as centered on problem-solving rather than simply designing new products, emphasizing that the organization is listening closely to what developers actually need most and shaping financing accordingly — whether that means adjusting timing, pricing, or loan terms to help projects overcome common barriers. The plan also calls for extending Housing Trust's first-time homebuyer programs into a wider geographic footprint across the region in the year ahead.Even before the 10-year plan was formalized, Housing Trust's broader work continued delivering tangible results across the Bay Area. In Sunnyvale, the organization provided a $2 million predevelopment loan in partnership with Related California to support Meridian Apartments, which created 90 affordable homes for families in one of the region's most expensive cities. In San Rafael, Housing Trust backed Eden Housing with a $4 million loan for Vivalon, a 66-unit affordable housing development for older adults that pairs affordable housing with supportive services.By the time of its 2025 Annual Report, marking its 25th anniversary, Housing Trust reported having invested more than $690 million total since its founding, helping create over 28,700 homes and open doors for roughly 53,800 neighbors across the greater Bay Area — figures that continue climbing as the MacKenzie Scott-funded plan moves into its early implementation phase.Housing Trust's gift wasn't an isolated act of generosity. MacKenzie Scott gave away roughly $2 billion in 2024 alone, spread across nearly 200 organizations focused largely on economic security, housing affordability, job stability, child development, and healthcare, bringing her five-year philanthropic total to more than $19 billion. Housing organizations across the country have been among her recurring areas of focus, with Housing Trust Silicon Valley standing as one of the more prominent recipients in that space.
Article Summary: The gift came through MacKenzie Scott's Yield Giving philanthropic fund and stood as the largest single donation from an individual in Housing Trust's history. The money could be used to strengthen its loan fund, expand existing housing programmes and launch new initiatives focused on affordability and housing equity.

Article Title: After jury finds Meta misled Facebook users over data privacy, New Mexico wants company to pay up to $40 billion in penalties
Article Text:
Tense hearing over penalties

‘Clash over constitutional limits and fines’

The state of New Mexico asked a state judge to order Meta to pay between $35 billion and $40 billion in civil penalties, following a jury verdict that found the tech giant repeatedly misled users about consumer privacy on Facebook. The request was made during a penalty hearing stemming from the fallout of the Cambridge Analytica controversy, as per a report by news agency Reuters. The British political consultancy, which worked on Donald Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign, harvested personal data from up to 87 million Facebook users via a third-party application without their explicit consent.The Santa Fe jury reached its liability verdict on September 25. State District Judge Francis Mathew, who presided over the proceedings, will determine the exact financial penalty Meta must pay.During the hearing, counsel for both sides argued over the scale of potential damages. Attorneys for Meta argued that the state's penalty demands were disproportionate to the specific conduct presented during the trial. Judge Mathew challenged that view from the bench, observing, “Well, when the parties go to trial, they roll the dice. They have to accept the consequences of their decision to go to trial, do they not?”The legal action, initially filed in 2021, alleged that Meta deceived Facebook users across New Mexico regarding data access permissions, internal enforcement policies, and the moderation of hate speech and misinformation.State prosecutors asserted that Meta was fully aware third parties enjoyed expansive access to private user information, and claimed the company tolerated toxic or harmful posts whenever doing so aided its financial performance.During the trial, jurors reviewed 29 distinct public assertions made by Meta and its executive leadership. The panel concluded that 26 out of the 29 statements were misleading. Jurors also determined Meta committed over 43 million individual violations of New Mexico’s consumer protection statutes, calculated from the audience size of state residents and local Facebook users exposed to each deceptive statement.Meta’s legal team pushed back during trial, arguing that state prosecutors cherry-picked isolated remarks. They added that the company had consistently acknowledged that its oversight of privacy and false content was imperfect.Under New Mexico law, the court holds discretion to levy civil fines up to $5,000 per violation.Randi McGinn, an attorney representing New Mexico, acknowledged in court that enforcing the statutory maximum of $5,000 across all 43 million violations would yield an excessively large figure under constitutional due process protections.However, McGinn urged the bench to deliver a financial penalty large enough to alter the company's behavior:“This court should speak to Meta in the only language it understands, which is money, and the value of its stock price,” McGinn argued.She said an award of $35 billion to $40 billion, which is about 205 of the statutory maximum allowed by the jury's findings, would affect company valuations but would be within constitutional due process limits.Meta counsel Matt Nicholson strongly contested the state's calculations, labeling the demand an "astronomical penalty that would obviously violate a host of constitutional provisions." In written court filings, Meta urged Judge Mathew to cap total penalties at $3.45 billion.
Article Summary: The state of New Mexico asked a state judge to order Meta to pay between $35 billion and $40 billion in civil penalties. The request was made during a penalty hearing stemming from the fallout of the Cambridge Analytica controversy. State District Judge Francis Mathew, who presided over the proceedings, will determine the exact financial penalty Meta must pay.

Article Title: Microsoft AI launches MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming alongside multilingual MAI-Voice 2.1 models
Article Text:
Real-time speech recognition: MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming

Natural Multilingual Output: MAI-Voice-2.1

MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash Low-Latency Scale

Microsoft has launched MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming model, with Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman, calling it the most accurate real-time audio transcription model in the world. Unveiled alongside two companion speech generation models – MAI-Voice-2.1 and the high-speed MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash – the release is designed to provide developers with responsive, low-cost building blocks for building autonomous conversational voice agents.According to Suleyman, the new voice architecture delivers inference speeds that are 55% faster and operational costs that are 60% cheaper than comparable offerings like ElevenLabs. He said in a post on X (formerly Twitter): “We're launching the most accurate real time transcription model in the world... #1 !!! 55% faster and 60% cheaper than ElevenLabs. Come build agents on our platform!”The headline addition to the company’s audio lineup, MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming, provides continuous, low-latency live speech-to-text across 60 languages with built-in automatic language detection. Key performance benchmarks and features include top benchmark ranking as the model has secured the No. 1 spot for accuracy across both partial and completed transcripts on the independent benchmark platform Artificial Analysis.It sits on the Pareto frontier for accuracy versus latency, eliminating the historical tradeoff where high precision required sluggish processing times. Instead of pausing until a sentence ends, the model outputs initial text hypotheses within roughly 100 milliseconds of receiving incoming audio.It refines words as additional context arrives and finalizes stable text immediately.By surfacing partial transcripts as words are spoken, voice bots can trigger API tools and start logical reasoning before the user finishes speaking. For live captioning and automated dictation workflows, internal tests show text appears on-screen twice as fast as the nearest market competitor.To pair with speech recognition, the team introduced MAI-Voice-2.1, its flagship multilingual text-to-speech engine covering 23 languages and 26 regional locales.The system's standout capability is cross-lingual identity preservation. A single synthetic voice persona can switch seamlessly between diverse languages, such as English, Mandarin and German, without carrying a foreign accent over from one language to another. Instead, the synthesized speaker modifies actual local pronunciation and retains a unique vocal identity.That means brands can deploy uniform virtual ambassadors worldwide, educational sites can switch languages while keeping the same instructors, and customer support agents can respond in the caller’s language without missing a beat.MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash was introduced by the company for mission-critical, high-capacity applications that demand immediate response times.The Flash version offers the same 23-language voice consistency as the base model, but it is optimized for high-throughput enterprise workloads, and can produce 45 seconds of synthesized audio with an end-to-end latency of just 150 milliseconds.
Article Summary: MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming is the most accurate real-time audio transcription model in the world, says Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman. The release is designed to provide developers with responsive, low-cost building blocks for building conversational voice agents.

Article Title: Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2026: India ranks 7th globally in customer hacking impacts
Article Text:
Three dominant trends defining modern cyber threats

Key data points: Phishing triples

According to the recently released Microsoft Digital Defense Report (MDDR) 2026, India was seventh globally in the countries where customers were most impacted by hacking in the first half of 2026. Drawing telemetry from more than 165 trillion daily security signals, the assessment highlights a threat landscape where malicious activity is moving with a faster speed, spreading across complex digital networks and narrowing the window organisations have to respond.The report identifies three fundamental shifts shaping digital defense today. The first is interconnected attack surfaces. Threat campaigns no longer remain isolated as modern hacking routinely pivots across user identities, business applications, multi-cloud platforms, third-party suppliers and physical critical infrastructure.The second is that artificial intelligence (AI) is expanding the operational scale of cyber activity on both sides. Both malicious actors and security analysts are deploying AI to accelerate decision cycles, optimise workflow efficiency, and shorten execution windows.Thirdly, user credentials are still the most abused entry point. Compromised login accounts are still used as a launchpad for wide-spread corporate infiltration and systematic operational disruption.Metrics released in the 2026 study demonstrate how fast a first breach can spread across an enterprise. In 2026, 23% of all recorded intrusions were the result of phishing campaigns, a sharp increase from the 7% recorded over the previous year.The report also notes that over 52% of compromised user account incidents resulted in secondary credential harvesting, showing just how fast one compromised user can put larger systems at risk.The time from public disclosure of a software vulnerability to its active exploitation in the wild often now falls well under 24 hours leaving defenders minimal time to deploy patches. As security incidents now cross organisational borders and supply chains in hours, Microsoft emphasised that building active organizational resilience is now just as critical as perimeter defense.
Article Summary: India was seventh globally in the countries where customers were most impacted by hacking in the first half of 2026. In 2026, 23% of all recorded intrusions were the result of phishing campaigns. The time from public disclosure of a software vulnerability to its active exploitation in the wild often now falls well under 24 hours.

Article Title: TRAI orders Reliance Jio, Airtel, Vodafone Idea to make mandatory recharge plans easier to find
Article Text:
What TRAI has ordered

Why TRAI stepped in

What these mandatory plans actually are

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has directed telecom operators to prominently display mandatory recharge plans and special tariff vouchers on their websites, mobile applications and exclusive points of sale, following complaints that such plans were difficult for consumers to locate. According to a report by PTI, in an order issued on Thursday, the regulator said all telecom service providers must create a separate and clearly visible section titled "TRAI-Mandated Packs" on their websites and mobile apps. The tab must appear as the first option in the prepaid recharge section and should also be prominently displayed at other exclusive sales channels.According to an official order published Thursday, telecom operators must create a separate, clearly visible tab or section titled "TRAI-Mandated Packs," containing the different types of TRAI-mandated vouchers. Crucially, this section must appear as the first tab under the prepaid recharge section of operator websites and apps, rather than being buried under other categories, and must also be prominently displayed at exclusive points of sale. Operators have been given 30 days to comply.The directive follows a wave of consumer complaints about poor transparency and difficulty navigating operator websites and apps to find these mandated plans.TRAI's own review of telecom websites and apps confirmed the problem, finding that mandated vouchers were often placed under unrelated categories or required users to click through multiple pages and screens before they could even be located.The regulator said improving visibility and accessibility would particularly benefit budget-conscious consumers, especially those with limited data needs or those in rural areas and feature-phone users, who are most likely to actually want and seek out these standalone, lower-cost plans.Existing TRAI rules already require every telecom operator to offer, at minimum, one Plan Voucher, one Special Tariff Voucher, and one Combo Voucher, each with a validity of 30 days, renewable on the same date every month. Separately, operators are also required to offer Special Tariff Vouchers exclusively for voice and SMS, without data bundled in, giving subscribers an option they can use even if they don't need mobile data — a category TRAI has pushed telcos to expand more aggressively across various validity periods in recent regulatory updates throughout the year.Importantly, this latest order doesn't introduce any new voucher category or change pricing — it's purely about visibility and accessibility, ensuring consumers can actually find the plans operators are already legally required to offer, rather than having to dig through confusing app menus to locate them.
Article Summary: TRAI has ordered telecom operators to prominently display mandatory recharge plans and special tariff vouchers on their websites, mobile applications and exclusive points of sale. The directive follows a wave of consumer complaints about poor transparency and difficulty navigating operator websites and apps to find these mandated plans. The regulator said improving visibility and accessibility would benefit budget-conscious consumers.

Article Title: Steve Jobs’ son watched his father battle cancer as a child; decades later, Reed Jobs is using a $1 billion fund to fight the disease
Article Text:
Reed Jobs’ childhood changed after Steve Jobs’ diagnosis

Yosemite now manages more than $1 billion

Reed Jobs wants cancer to become manageable

The Yosemite name has a personal connection

Reed Jobs was 12 when his father, Apple co-founder Steve Jobs, was diagnosed with a rare form of pancreatic cancer. Eight years later, Steve died at 56, while Reed was an undergraduate at Stanford. The experience shaped Reed’s interest in cancer research, leading him to spend summers working in oncology laboratories as a teenager before eventually moving into healthcare investing. In 2023, he launched Yosemite, an oncology-focused investment firm that combines venture capital with philanthropic funding. Yosemite initially launched with more than $200 million. By early 2026, the firm had raised another $200 million-plus for its second fund and said it was managing more than $1 billion in assets.Reed became interested in cancer after seeing his father diagnosed when he was 12. Steve Jobs had been diagnosed with a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour, a rare form of pancreatic cancer. Reed later spent time working in oncology laboratories at Stanford as a teenager and initially entered Stanford as a pre-med student.Steve Jobs died on October 5, 2011, at the age of 56. Reed was 20 at the time and was studying at Stanford.After his father's death, Reed changed his major from pre-med to history. He eventually returned to healthcare through his work at Emerson Collective, the impact-investing and philanthropic organisation founded by his mother, Laurene Powell Jobs.Before creating Yosemite, Reed spent years working at Emerson Collective, where he focused on health and cancer-related initiatives. Yosemite emerged from that work and became an independent organisation in 2023.The firm announced its first close of more than $200 million in August 2023. Its model combines traditional venture investment with philanthropic grants for academic researchers. The aim is to support scientific work at an early stage and help promising discoveries develop into treatments and companies.Yosemite focuses exclusively on oncology and has invested in areas including gene therapy, immunotherapy, cancer vaccines, radiopharmaceuticals, artificial intelligence-powered drug discovery and earlier cancer detection.Yosemite's financial scale has grown substantially since its launch. In January 2026, the San Francisco Chronicle reported that the firm had raised more than $200 million for its second fund and was seeking an additional $150 million. The new fund was backed by institutions and investors including Amgen, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, MIT and John Doerr.Forbes reported that Yosemite's second fund was targeting $350 million. Following its latest funding round, the firm said it managed more than $1 billion in assets, including money overseen for hospitals, endowments and foundations.The firm's own announcement said its second fund had initially closed at more than $200 million and that Yosemite now managed more than $1 billion in assets.Reed has described a long-term goal of changing how cancer is treated. In an interview reported by the San Francisco Chronicle, he said he believes many cancers could eventually move from being fatal diagnoses to manageable, chronic diseases within his lifetime. Yosemite's current investments reflect that strategy. The firm has backed companies working on technologies ranging from gene therapies and cancer vaccines to AI-assisted drug discovery. According to the San Francisco Chronicle, Yosemite was invested in about 20 companies and expected its new fund to support around 25 companies.The name of Reed's firm also comes from an important chapter in his family's history. Steve Jobs and Laurene Powell Jobs married on March 18, 1991, at the Ahwahnee Hotel in Yosemite National Park. The ceremony was attended by about 50 people, and the wedding included a vegan cake shaped like Half Dome. The couple also went hiking after the ceremony. Reed was born in September 1991, months after his parents' wedding. He was their first child, followed by daughters Erin and Eve.Reed's career has therefore come full circle. His interest in oncology began during his father's illness, continued through his teenage work in cancer laboratories and later became part of his professional work at Emerson Collective.
Article Summary: Reed Jobs was 12 when his father, Apple co-founder Steve Jobs, was diagnosed with a rare form of pancreatic cancer. The experience shaped Reed’s interest in cancer research, leading him to spend summers working in oncology laboratories as a teenager. In 2023, he launched Yosemite, an oncologist-focused investment firm that combines venture capital with philanthropic funding. By early 2026, the firm had raised another $200 million-plus for its second fund and said it was managing more than $1 billion in assets.

Article Title: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon once again 'warns' Europe 'you may be losing', offers 'big, beautiful solution'
Article Text:
Jamie Dimon calls for deeper economic integration

What Europe needs to fix, according to Jamie Dimon

Vision for a stronger Western alliance

Not the first time JPMorgan CEO delivered this message

Jamie Dimon, the CEO of America’s largest bank JPMorgan Chase has renewed his warning that Europe risks falling behind economically, while proposing what he called a ‘big beautiful’ free-trade agreement with the United States as part of a broader effort to strengthen the Western alliance. In an opinion piece published in The Wall Street Journal, Dimon argued that Washington should offer Europe a sweeping economic partnership if the continent implements meaningful economic and military reforms designed to boost growth, competitiveness and security. “I believe the U.S. should offer Europe a major inducement: If it executes meaningful economic and military reforms... the US will negotiate one big, beautiful economic and free-trade agreement with Europe,” Dimon wrote.According to Dimon, such an agreement would go beyond Europe and could eventually be extended to friendly democracies including Canada, Mexico, Japan, South Korea, Australia and the Philippines.He described deeper economic integration among democratic allies as a potential “game changer” that would allow them to set global trade rules, strengthen economic resilience and present a united front against geopolitical pressures.Dimon's proposal contrasts with the more protectionist approach adopted by the administration of Donald Trump, whose tariff policies have strained relations with several trading partners, including the European Union and Canada.Dimon's op-ed didn't just float a vague aspiration — it named specific reforms he believes are prerequisites. He called on the European Union to finally complete its long-delayed Capital Markets Union and Banking Union to boost competitiveness, to follow through on the recommendations laid out in the Draghi report, and to secure genuine independence in defense, manufacturing, and energy.He argued that a Europe capable of mobilizing capital, scaling innovative companies, consolidating defense production, and reducing strategic dependencies would emerge as a stronger security partner, a more resilient economic partner, and a more credible counterweight to China's growing economic influence.Beyond Europe, Dimon argued that the United States must also take steps to preserve its position as the world's leading economic and military power. He called for renewed focus on strengthening the American economy, expanding opportunity and reinforcing democratic alliances.According to Dimon, a combination of US leadership and successful European reforms could create a stronger Western bloc capable of driving economic growth and addressing long-term geopolitical challenges.“A renewed commitment to American values and alliances coupled with bold reforms by Europe would be a geopolitical and economic home run, guaranteeing the Western world's strength for the next 250 years,” he wrote.This isn't the first time Dimon has bluntly criticized Europe's economic standing. Last year, speaking to European business and political leaders at an event in Ireland, he delivered an even more direct version of the same warning, telling the room flatly that, compared with the US and Asia, Europe is losing.
Article Summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has called for a 'big beautiful' free-trade agreement with the United States. Dimon argued that Washington should offer Europe a sweeping economic partnership if the continent implements meaningful economic and military reforms. According to Dimon, such an agreement would go beyond Europe and could eventually be extended to friendly democracies including Canada, Mexico and Japan.

Article Title: In 2010, Elon Musk funded a 25-kilowatt solar system for an Alabama disaster centre; 108 panels and battery backup were designed to keep it powered when the surrounding grid went down
Article Text:
“This seemed like a good thing to do to help people out, while simultaneously creating awareness that there was a better way to keep things going than just ‘drill, baby, drill,”

A solar system for a community recovering from disasters

“Electricity bills are a big deal for a community center like ours when you have to pay for it out-of-pocket,”

“But all of a sudden now we have solar power! For a little area that no one has ever heard about, that’s amazing.”

The project led to wider solar efforts

Elon Musk funded a solar project in Alabama in 2010. The 25-kilowatt system, installed at the South Bay Communities Alliance (SBCA) Hurricane Response Center in Coden, Alabama, was designed to help the facility keep operating if a disaster knocked out the surrounding electricity grid. The installation included 108 photovoltaic panels and battery backup and was expected to provide about 90% to 100% of the centre’s electricity needs. Musk’s foundation provided the funding, while solar company SolarCity donated and installed the system. The project came as Coden was still dealing with the effects of Hurricane Katrina and the Deepwater Horizon oil spill, which had affected the coastal community’s commercial fishing industry.Musk said the project was intended to help residents while demonstrating an alternative to dependence on oil.said Musk, who also runs the electric car company Tesla Motors.Coden was a coastal community where commercial fishing had been an important source of employment.The Deepwater Horizon disaster added another setback to an area that was already recovering from Hurricane Katrina. More than 100 families in the community were still waiting to rebuild their homes after the hurricane.The SBCA Hurricane Response Center served as a gathering and response point for the local community. The solar installation was intended to keep the centre powered during emergencies, when a damaged grid could leave residents without electricity.The system was also expected to reduce the centre’s regular electricity costs.says Zack Carter, an organiser for SBCA.The battery backup was important because this project was more than just producing power in the normal way. It was supposed to provide energy security if a hurricane or other disaster knocked out the local power grid.The Coden installation became an early disaster-relief project involving SolarCity and the Musk Foundation. The organisations later worked on a similar solar project in Japan following the 2011 Fukushima nuclear disaster. In 2012, SolarCity also worked with partners to provide portable solar power stations for communities affected by Hurricane Sandy.By then, SolarCity’s philanthropy had expanded well beyond disaster relief. In 2013, the company launched the GivePower Foundation to provide electricity to schools in developing countries without reliable power.By 2014, GivePower said it had helped 511 schools in Africa and Central America, exceeding its original target of 400 schools. Its projects used solar panels, batteries and lights, while teams also trained local residents to troubleshoot the equipment and maintain the systems.The organisation's projects included schools in Mali, Nicaragua and Kenya. In Kenya, a school in the village of Kirindon could use laptops donated by Intel after receiving a solar installation.For Coden, however, the original project had a more immediate purpose. The combination of 108 solar panels and battery storage was intended to give a disaster response centre a source of electricity that could continue working even when the surrounding grid could not.
Article Summary: Elon Musk funded a solar project in Alabama in 2010. The 25-kilowatt system was designed to help the facility keep operating if a disaster knocked out the surrounding electricity grid. The installation included 108 photovoltaic panels and battery backup and was expected to provide about 90% to 100% of the centre's electricity needs.
